article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

tasks.prompt: What opportunity and challenge does the article examine?
options: Replacing every lithium-ion battery in smartphones this year
Building a US sodium-ion battery industry using local materials while competing with China's manufacturing lead
Ending renewable-energy storage projects
Importing all future batteries from Europe
tasks.correct_answer: Building a US sodium-ion battery industry using local materials while competing with China's manufacturing lead
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה בוחנת את האפשרות לבנות בארה״ב תעשיית סוללות נתרן־יון מחומרים מקומיים, לצד פערי עלות, קנה מידה ותחרות מול סין.

tasks.prompt: Why are sodium-ion batteries attractive for stationary energy storage?
options: They have the highest energy density for tiny phones.
They may be cheaper, tolerate a wider temperature range and require less cooling.
They contain no electrolyte or electrodes.
They can generate electricity without being charged.
tasks.correct_answer: They may be cheaper, tolerate a wider temperature range and require less cooling.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: לסוללות נתרן־יון יש פוטנציאל לעלות נמוכה, פעולה בטווח טמפרטורות רחב וצורכי קירור קטנים יותר—יתרונות חשובים לאגירה נייחת.

tasks.prompt: What does “floundered” mean when the article discusses earlier US battery companies?
options: Expanded without difficulty
Received automatic certification
Struggled and failed to make steady progress
Moved all production to Michigan
tasks.correct_answer: Struggled and failed to make steady progress
tasks.explanation_hebrew: floundered פירושו התקשה ולא הצליח להתקדם באופן יציב; הכתבה מציינת שחברות אמריקאיות בתחום נכשלו או הסתבכו בעבר.

tasks.prompt: What safety concern was raised about Unigrid's cathode material?
options: Sodium can never store electricity.
The cathode contains no active material.
The battery works only below freezing.
Under some conditions chromium-3 might form toxic, cancer-causing chromium-6.
tasks.correct_answer: Under some conditions chromium-3 might form toxic, cancer-causing chromium-6.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: המחלוקת נוגעת לאפשרות שבתנאים מסוימים כרום־3 שבקתודה יהפוך לכרום־6 רעיל ומסרטן.

tasks.prompt: How did Unigrid respond to the chromium safety concern?
options: It admitted the battery had never been tested.
It said the concern was overblown and cited certification and tests that did not produce chromium-6.
It stopped selling every battery immediately.
It removed all voltage controls from the system.
tasks.correct_answer: It said the concern was overblown and cited certification and tests that did not produce chromium-6.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: Unigrid טענה שהחשש מוגזם, הדגישה בדיקות והסמכה לאירופה ואמרה שבדיקות צד שלישי לא הצליחו ליצור כרום־6.

tasks.prompt: Why are sodium-ion batteries more likely to dominate large storage systems than smartphones?
options: Large systems never need safety certification.
Phones cannot use rechargeable batteries.
Lower energy density makes sodium-ion cells larger and heavier for the same power, which matters less in stationary systems.
Sodium-ion batteries operate only inside data centres.
tasks.correct_answer: Lower energy density makes sodium-ion cells larger and heavier for the same power, which matters less in stationary systems.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: צפיפות האנרגיה הנמוכה מחייבת סוללה גדולה וכבדה יותר; החיסרון משמעותי בטלפון אך פחות קריטי במתקן אגירה קבוע.

tasks.prompt: Give three ways US start-ups hope to build a domestic sodium-ion battery industry.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין שלוש אסטרטגיות או תוכניות קונקרטיות מן הכתבה ולזהות את החברה או היעד כשאפשר.
expected_points: Unigrid hopes eventually to source sodium-ion cells in the US.
Emerald Battery Labs is developing vehicle auxiliary batteries and new anodes for US-made cells.
Peak Energy and GM aim to build a US supply chain and a Michigan facility by the end of 2028.
Alsym plans to ship hundreds of megawatt hours of US-made batteries by 2027.
Companies target grid storage, data centres and commercial fleets rather than only consumer electronics.
US production could use locally sourced materials and reduce supply-chain dependence.

tasks.prompt: Why does relying on China-sourced cells both help and weaken the US start-ups' strategy?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר את היתרון לטווח הקצר ואת הסתירה מול יעד הייצור המקומי והעצמאות בשרשרת האספקה.
expected_points: Chinese cells let start-ups reach customers and test products sooner.
China already has manufacturing scale and technical experience.
Using imported cells reduces the initial capital and time needed to launch.
Dependence on China conflicts with the goal of a domestic US supply chain.
Future US cells may cost more, so switching suppliers creates commercial uncertainty.
The arrangement can be a bridge while local factories and materials develop.

tasks.prompt: Summarise the case for sodium-ion batteries and the main obstacles facing US producers.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: הסיכום צריך לכלול יתרונות טכנולוגיים וכלכליים, שימושים מתאימים, סוגיות בטיחות, תחרות מסין ואתגרי עלות וייצור.
expected_points: Sodium-ion batteries may use abundant local materials, cost less and work across a wide temperature range.
They may reduce cooling needs and support homes, grids and data centres.
Their lower energy density makes them less suitable for small devices.
Cathode chemistry, fire risk, longevity and certification still require careful testing.
China currently leads cell manufacturing, and several US firms still rely on Chinese cells.
Current sodium-ion prices can exceed cheap LFP batteries, while mass production remains difficult.
US start-ups see domestic demand and renewable-energy storage as an opportunity.

tasks.prompt: Using evidence from the article, assess whether the US should support domestic sodium-ion battery production.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג הערכה מאוזנת, להשתמש בלפחות ארבע ראיות מן הכתבה ולדון בביטחון אנרגטי, עלות, בטיחות, ייצור ויישומים.
expected_points: Domestic production could reduce dependence on foreign materials and manufacturing.
Local sodium-based supply chains may improve energy security and support renewable storage.
Data-centre and grid demand could provide a large market.
US firms face China's scale advantage and uncertain production costs.
Cheap LFP batteries currently compete strongly on price.
Chromium chemistry and fire risks show the need for independent testing and certification.
Lower energy density limits some markets but not stationary storage.
Support could be conditional on safety, domestic sourcing milestones and demonstrated commercial reliability.
